senses.sense_definition: The demographic trend or process in which people migrate from urban centers to the countryside.

examples.text: The widespread adoption of remote work has sparked a trend of <w>ruralization</w> among young professionals.
Economic instability in major cities led to a steady <w>ruralization</w> across several southern provinces.

senses.sense_definition: The act or process of making an area, culture, or economy more rural in character.

examples.text: The regime enforced the radical <w>ruralization</w> of society by forcing city residents onto collective farms.
Planners debated whether the preservation policy contributed to the unwanted <w>ruralization</w> of the industrial zone.

senses.sense_definition: The historical process involving the decline of cities and the development of village settlements.

examples.text: Following the collapse of the empire, a gradual <w>ruralization</w> reshaped the landscape into scattered agrarian communities.
Historians study the post-classical <w>ruralization</w> that followed the abandonment of major Roman trade hubs.

senses.sense_definition: The proportion of a population residing in villages and countryside communities, or the rate of its increase.

examples.text: The government report measured the rate of <w>ruralization</w> across several underdeveloped regions.
High levels of <w>ruralization</w> often correlate with economies that rely predominantly on subsistence agriculture.
